summary: Michael Kowalewski works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter (1947–2020) was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He served at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1982 and 2020) and was a research fellow at Lumbini International Research Institute (attested 2000).

Michael Lessman specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from Georgetown University (BA, 2010–2014), the Catholic University of America (MA, 2014–2017), and the University of Munich (MA, 2017–2019), and became a doctoral candidate at Yale University in 2019.

Michael M. Ames (1933–2006) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. After completing degrees at the University of British Columbia and Harvard University under Cora Du Bois, he taught at McMaster University and UBC, where he directed the Museum of Anthropology (1974–1997).
Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge around 1965–1969 and held an academic post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Meier-Brügger (born 1948) is a linguist who studied under Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich (~1967–1973). He held a post at the Free University of Berlin from around 1996 to 2013.
Michael Oppitz (born 1942) is a scholar in Tibetology. He held a position at the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1988–1989) and served as director (Leiter) at the University of Zurich (~1990–2008).

Michael P. Berman specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His career includes posts attested in 2012 as a professor at Brock University and managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.
Michael Pakenham Edgeworth (1812–1881) studied at Charterhouse School and the University of Edinburgh (~1827–1829). He worked in Indology and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1831 to 1859.

Michael Puett (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1987–1994) under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu, and has held professorships at Harvard University (~1994, ~2013).

Michael Pye (born 1939) is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and Leeds under Maurice Wiles, he held posts at Leeds (~1968–1978), Marburg (1982–2004), Lancaster (1991–1994), and Otani University (~2004–2007).

Michael Radich, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his PhD at Harvard (~2001–2007). He taught at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and held posts at Kyoto University (2009), Hamburg (2013–2014), and Heidelberg University (appointed 2018).
Michael S. Drummond works in Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1979, 1992, attested 2008), the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Michael Schonken is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned an MS at California State University, Fullerton (2013–2015). He taught at Beijing Royal School (2017–2021) and Nord Anglia School Beijing (2021–2024), becoming a PhD student at Tsinghua University in 2024.

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under Steven D. Goodman (attested 2007) and became Director of Research at the University of Virginia in 2018.

Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (~1962–1972). He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from around 1971 to 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA under Stephen R. Bokenkamp at Indiana University Bloomington. He has held positions at the Max Planck Institute, University of Leipzig, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much (born 1953) is a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner and held a fellowship at the University of Hamburg.

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen (1838–1847). He served at Copenhagen University Library (1861) and held a professorship at the University of Copenhagen from 1878 to 1902.
